thinkers.name: Aris Roussinos
thinkers.why: Originating UnHerd essay; still the cleanest short definition.
thinkers.guardrail: Journalist, not a mascot. Quote him, do not enlist him.

thinkers.name: Peter Diamandis
thinkers.one_line: Techno-optimist who argues exponential technologies can meet large human problems.
thinkers.why: An anchor for Anglofuturism's hyper-ambitions — abundance as an engineering claim, not a vibe.
thinkers.guardrail: American abundance talk. Steal the altitude, not the Californian costume.

thinkers.name: Dominic Cummings
thinkers.one_line: State capacity, elite performance, and high-throughput science.
thinkers.why: A policy engine: how a state that can still do things would actually be wired.
thinkers.guardrail: A former operator, not a saint. Read the method, not the memoir war.

thinkers.name: David Starkey
thinkers.one_line: Argues the English constitutional apparatus was an engine of global modernity.
thinkers.why: Historical grounding: law and parliament as technologies, not costume drama.
thinkers.guardrail: Historian with a polemic. Take the constitutional claim; leave the chat-show heat.

thinkers.name: Wyndham Lewis
thinkers.why: Founded the Vorticists — a modernist avant-garde rooted in an Anglo temperament, not Milanese theatre.
thinkers.guardrail: Aesthetic ancestor only. BLAST is a magazine, not a political programme.

thinkers.name: Sam Bowman
thinkers.one_line: Makes an Anglofuturist vision physically viable.
thinkers.why: Articulates the materialist, supply-side backbone of British techno-optimism.
thinkers.guardrail: Economist, not a movement officer. Numbers before slogans.
